To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a BMI reduction of at least 0.42 kg/m2 or a WC reduction at least of 3.0 cm during a 1-year period in men with micro- and macroalbuminuria at baseline was associated with a reduced incidence of these conditions at the 1 year follow up.
changes in BMI and WC were associated with the incidence of CKD.
changes in obesity parameters are associated with the incidence of chronic kidney disease (i.e., micro-/macroalbumiuria and low estimated glomerulafiltration rate) in Japanese individuals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between changes in obesity parameters and the incidence of CKD in Japanese individuals.
the importance of lowering the BMI and WC of men with micro-/ macroalbuminuria to prevent the appearance or worsening of CKD.
the association between changes in obesity parameters and the incidence of CKD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the incidence of CKD components is reduced by lowering obesity indexes in men, but the incidence of CKDs is increased by increasing obesity indexes in men without microalbuminuria and/or a low eGFr at the first examination.
the reduction in obesity indexes in men is a good preventive measure for CKD.
a BMI increase or a WC gain over a 1-year period in individuals with normal renal function increases the risk of micro-/macroalbu-minuria and low eGFR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the reduction of obesity in individuals who already have micro-/macroalbumuria is beneficial for reducing the risk of CKD, whereas the increase of BMI in individuals without CKD at baseline is a risk factor for CKD.
obesity control is important in the management of CKD.
the reduction of the obesity indexes, BMI or WC in men with micro/macroalbuminuria at baseline reduced the incidence of micro/macroalbumininuria during the 1 year follow-up.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reduction in obesity indexes in individuals with micro-/macroalbuninuria at the baseline screening is associated with a decreased risk of micro-/macroalburninuria at the follow-up screening.
changes in BMI or WC over the short term can be used as a risk marker for the incidence of CKD.
the changes in obesity indexes over 1 year are associated with the appearance and disappearance of the CKDs in Japanese individuals.
